items.title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense
items.summary: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is the standard paradigm for customizing large language models, yet third-party LoRA adapters pose a supply-chain risk: modifying less than 1% of model parameters suffices to implant stealthy backdoors. Recent defenses project adapter weights onto estimated backdoor subspaces, reporting near-zero static Attack Success Rates (ASR). We audit subspace-projection defenses across four model scales (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B) and three architectures (Qwen2.5, InternLM2.5, Spark). Constructively, module-wise rank-1 trigger-difference projection (k=1, alpha=1) reduces ASR from 60.4% to 0.0% on standard benchmarks and from 70.3% to 0.0% on a 1,000-sample uncontaminated suite (p = 3.055e-299, instruction-level p = 9.49e-16) in under 5 seconds end-to-end, and we prove via a spectral-gap bound why trigger-free calibration with benign polite suffixes aligns with u1(B) (median cosine 0.9048) and achieves 0.0% ASR without prior trigger knowledge. Our main contribution is a negative finding: static ASR reduction does not imply parameter erasure. Under 5-sample few-shot reactivation, every evaluated weight-editing defense rebounds (91.7%-100.0% ASR in 1 epoch for standard projections, Fine-Pruning, ANP, SVD truncation and Li & Kim's dual-end projection; 48.7% for our single-round dual variant), all reaching 100.0% by Epoch 2, with first-epoch loss up to 5.7x lower than training from scratch. Using an exact spectrum-preserving Haar orthogonal rotation control (Frobenius norm 10.0928 preserved to 1.70e-6) and N=1..6 cumulative Gram-Schmidt basis ablation, we decompose reactivation into residual trigger-difference coupling energy at Epoch 1 (Spearman rho = 0.986), base-model learnability at Epoch 2 (100%), and benign semantic direction conflict (41.7%).

items.title: Marginal utility, matrix factorization, and the Key-Value (KV) cache: a unified information-economic framework for sovereign geo-mining inference
items.summary: This paper builds a theoretical bridge between the economic notion of marginal utility and two machine-learning constructs, matrix factorization and the Key--Value cache of transformer language models. The singular value spectrum of a rating matrix is shown to be a diminishing marginal utility schedule for latent factors, the eigenvalue spectrum of the projected covariance operator to be the marginal utility schedule of a model's learned representation, and cache eviction and low-rank cache compression to be instances of constrained utility maximization under a memory budget. The three collapse into a single allocation rule: retain the top dimensions whose eigenvalue exceeds the shadow price of the binding constraint. The framework is applied to the automated extraction of structured information from geo-mining documents, where it motivates a multi-pass inference protocol, a layer-wise TIES model merging procedure, and a selection policy combining extraction quality, localization drift and energy, scalarized with a Conditional Value-at-Risk term on drift. Two empirical contributions are reported. An 11.2-million-parameter hierarchical classifier, trained in about five minutes on a single GPU, reaches 90.0 per cent level-1 accuracy on a held-out test set from a 973-document uranium-exploration corpus, against 92.0 per cent for a proprietary model on a fifty-document human audit of the same corpus, at a latency of 2.62 ms per card against approximately 2,000 ms for the API and at negligible cost. A diagnostic of uniform-density TIES merging exposes a reproducible degenerate mode in which the merged model returns token-identical outputs across five geographically distinct districts while declaring high confidence; re-executing the merge under layer-wise calibrated densities removes that signature on the diagnostic sample. The full-scale extraction benchmark, including LoRA fine-tuning, is reported as projected rather than measured and remains an empirical extension of this work.

items.title: MLoRA:Continual Low-Rank Adaptation via Relative-Response Subspace Selection and Momentum Orthogonalization
items.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) provides a parameter-efficient approach to continual learning, but its nominal rank can conceal a loss of effective adaptation capacity. We identify \emph{spectral plasticity collapse}: during sequential adaptation, update energy becomes concentrated in a small subset of singular modes, leaving much of the available low-rank space underutilized. This exposes a limitation of interference avoidance alone: protecting historical representations does not ensure that the remaining adaptation capacity is responsive to new tasks or effectively utilized. To address this problem, we propose \texttt{MLoRA}, which jointly controls capacity allocation and utilization. First, historical whitening identifies input directions with strong current-task response relative to accumulated historical response, yielding a task-adaptive basis that remains fixed during training. Second, approximate polar orthogonalization of momentum updates reduces spectral concentration within theselected space. An orthonormal basis connects these mechanisms by transferring the factor-update spectrum exactly tothe induced weight update. We establish a max--min characterization of exact subspace selection and derive cumulative spectral bounds under controlled cross-step anisotropy. Across five class-incremental benchmarks and eight incremental settings, \texttt{MuLoRA} achieves the highest mean accuracy in 15 of 16 reported metrics.

items.title: FireGate: Bounding Behaviour Change Before Training in Continual RL Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Fine-tuning a deployed language model on one task after another can change behaviour that should stay fixed, such as earlier skills, general chat or refusals. Today, such forgetting is found only after training, on the benchmarks someone chose to run. This work bounds, before training, how often its outputs change on chosen prompt distributions. FireGate places each task's update, such as a new LoRA, behind a gate, which is a classifier on the model's frozen lower layers that decides for each prompt whether the update is used. Where no gate fires, the model computes exactly what the old one computes. As a result, on any prompt distribution, every bounded behaviour score changes by at most the gates' firing rate there over a whole task stream. Calibrating each gate on unlabeled prompts of what must not change fixes that rate before training, with a PAC guarantee, whatever weights training produces. Forgetting is thus bounded by the gate's false-alarm rate, and its price is the gate's power: no update, gated or not, that changes as few protected outputs can change new-task outputs more often than the best test of that level tells new-task prompts from protected ones. On reinforcement-learning streams of up to five tasks, gated training keeps the earlier tasks and changes 3.3% of held-out chat responses, whereas ungated training changes 91.8%. Across seven models, the gain kept behind the gate follows its firing rate on new-task prompts, measured before training. The certificate covers the gated model as deployed, on the prompt distributions sampled for calibration, not against an adversary who searches for prompts that fire the gate.

items.title: RBA: A Read-out Basis Adapter for Parameter-Efficient Interactive OCTA Vessel Segmentation with SEEM
items.summary: Retinal disease monitoring with optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) relies on segmentation of vessels and the foveal avascular zone (FAZ). Promptable models such as SEEM (Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once) allow click-based refinement, but without adaptation SEEM segments thin vessels poorly and needs many clicks. Fully fine-tuning its 342 million parameters on a few hundred images is costly and risks overfitting, and parameter-efficient methods such as low-rank adaptation (LoRA) usually adapt only the encoder. Yet SEEM reads every candidate mask from one feature map at quarter resolution, too coarse for vessels one to three pixels wide. This study introduces the Read-out Basis Adapter (RBA), whose read-out branch generates 32 image-specific basis maps at half resolution. Each candidate accesses them through its own vector and a zero-initialised projection, so the model starts exactly as SEEM. The encoder branch, a standard rank-1 LoRA, supplies the information needed to tell arteries from veins. RBA adds 0.47 million trainable parameters. Under simulated error-driven clicks, with the ground truth used only to place them, RBA outperforms LoRA, Conv-LoRA andAdaptFormer on OCTA-500 3mmlarge vessels. Averaged over three seeds, it reaches an intersection over union (IoU) of 85.16% and a Dice score of 91.93%, 2.90 and 1.72 percentage points above Conv-LoRA. On the 6 mm subset, one run gives margins of 4.35 and 2.76 points. The gain extends to arteries, veins and ROSE-O but not to the FAZ. In SEEM, adaptation capacity pays more at the mask read-out than in the encoder.

items.title: Cách nấu phở bò truyền thống, chuẩn vị Hà Nội - Báo VnExpress Cooking
items.summary:
Ninh từ nước lạnh:Cho xương, hành gừng, sá sùng, túi gia vị vào nồi rồi đổ nước lạnh ngập mặt xương 5–7 cm. Nấu ở lửa nhỏ, không đậy nắp. Hớt bọt và hớt mỡ thường xuyên để nước trong. Lưu ý, không để sôi mạnh vì sẽ khiến nước đục. 

Thời gian ninh:6–8 giờ.

Nêm nước mắm đúng thời điểm: Chỉ cho nước mắm trước khi ăn 30 phút. Cho quá sớm sẽ át mùi phở, tạo mùi nồng. [...] Nướng hành, gừng và rang gia vị để tạo chiều su mùi: Nướng hành ty, hành khô, gừng. Hành khô chín nhanh nên lấy ra sớm tránh cháy đen. Gừng nướng đến khi thơm, vỏ sém. Rang quế, hồi, thảo quả ở lửa vừa 2-3 phút cho dậy mùi. Cho tất cả vào túi vải hoặc quả cầu inox để dễ lọc. Nướng rễ hành – rễ mùi ta. Đy là chi tiết nhỏ nhưng tạo hương phở Hà Nội đúng kiểu xưa.

 

Kỹ thuật hầm xương:Nồi nước dùng gồm 3 phần: 3 phần nước xương bò, 1 phần nước xương lợn, nước luộc thịt bò. [...] Chan phở:Xếp lần lượt bánh, thịt, hành. Múc một muôi đầy hành lá, hành trắng, chan nước sôi già lên để làm chín. Cuối cùng mới rưới chút mỡ bò nổi trên mặt nồi (nếu thích).

Gia vị ăn kèm:

Phở Bắc: dùng tương ớt, giấm tỏi.

Phở bò miền Bắc và miền Nam khác nhau thế nào?

Phở Bắc:

 Nước dùng: trong, thanh, không ngọt sắc
 Gia vị khô dùng ít, hương thoang thoảng
 Bánh phở nhỏ, mềm
 Ăn kèm quẩy
 Không rau sống đa dạng

items.title: Cách nấu phở bò truyền thống: Bí quyết nước dùng trong vắt
items.summary:
Đun sôi một nồi nước riêng, cho lượng bánh phở vừa đủ vào vá lưới và trụng khoảng 10 – 15 giây. Xốc nhẹ cho ráo nước rồi cho bánh phở vào tô. Xếp bắp bò thái lát lên trên, thêm thịt bò tái thái mỏng nếu muốn thưởng thức phở tái.

Tiếp tục cho hành lá, ngò gai, đầu hành và hành tây thái mỏng vào tô. Đun nước dùng sôi nóng rồi chan trực tiếp vào tô, đặc biệt chú ý phần thịt bò tái để thịt chín vừa tới. Dùng phở ngay khi còn nóng, có thể ăn kèm chanh, ớt, tương đen hoặc tương ớt tùy khẩu vị. [...] Nướng hành và gừng:Nướng hành tây, gừng trên bếp đến khi phần ngoài hơi cháy xém và dậy mùi thơm. Sau đó cạo bỏ phần cháy, rửa sạch và đập dập nhẹ.

   Rang gia vị:Cho hoa hồi, quế, thảo quả, đinh hương và hạt mùi vào chảo khô, rang ở lửa nhỏ khoảng 3 – 4 phút đến khi thơm.

   Cho vào túi lọc:Để gia vị nguội bớt rồi cho vào túi vải hoặc túi lọc sạch, buộc kín để thuận tiện khi cho vào nồi nước dùng.

Image 151: Nướng hành tây, gừng trên bếp

Nướng hành tây, gừng trên bếp [...] Hoa hồi:3 – 4 tai.

   Quế thanh: 1 – 2 thanh, mỗi thanh khoảng 5cm.

   Thảo quả:2 quả, đập dập trước khi nấu.

   Đinh hương:5 – 6 nụ.

   Hạt mùi: 1 muỗng canh.

   Gia vị nêm:Muối, nước mắm và đường.

items.title: Scaling AI-driven chip design with open agent factories - IBM Research
items.summary: AI for chip design connects two forms of progress into a reciprocal relationship: Better hardware enables more capable AI, and more capable AI can help engineers develop better hardware. Cost-efficient agent factories make that relationship more practical. By making each search more affordable, open models and distributed inference create room to test more ideas and, with better search strategies, turn that opportunity into better chips. [...] As AI systems become more capable, researchers are increasingly asking a practical question: Can AI do more than help write code for computing systems? Specifically, can it actively participate in the design of complex computing systems and rapidly translate algorithms into silicon? New work in AI-driven chip design suggests the answer is yes. But a promising algorithm is only the beginning of a hardware design. Turning it into an efficient chip requires exploring how to organize computation, [...] The results also suggest that the practical value of AI-assisted chip design depends on more than the best design an agent can produce. It also depends on how much verified exploration an organization can afford. Model capability, the assignment of agent roles, and the infrastructure serving those models all shape the hardware improvements that are attainable within a real engineering budget. items.title: Microsoft will mainly use its Maia chips for AI inference
items.summary:
The emerging opportunity in chips stems from unrelenting demand for advanced processors and a desire in the market for choice. Nvidia's GPUs have been the standard for AI workloads and models, and they fill Microsoft's existing data centers, while also serving to train models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

But as demand keeps growing, the model leaders have embraced a variety of silicon from companies including Amazon, Advanced Micro Devices, Cerebras, Google and, in recent months, Microsoft. [...] Microsoft introduced its inaugural AI chip, the Maia 100, in 2023. It touted the Maia 200 this past January, and CEO Satya Nadella told analysts in July that Maia 200 "delivers 30% better performance per dollar than the latest generation hardware in our fleet" and said it was handling OpenAI models.

items.title: Google's chip business is on a faster track than Nvidia's own AI boom
items.summary:
Google introduced two new tensor processing units, or TPUs — its homegrown AI chips — on Monday. The TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max join the 8t and 8i it unveiled in April, the first time Google has introduced four TPU systems in a single year. Both new chips ship next year. [...] Think of it as a chip menu. The 8tx keeps data encrypted for governments, banks, and other regulated businesses, paired with processors from AMD (AMD). The 8i Max squeezes two chips into one package for requests with long context windows — the amount of information an AI model can juggle at once. [...] Google is selling on price. SemiAnalysis found that Google's current Ironwood TPU delivers up to nearly three times as much AI output per dollar as Nvidia's Blackwell chips when running AI agents, though Nvidia's top system still wins when speed is everything.
